src/infrastructure/uuid-id-generator.ts: `class UuidIdGenerator implements IdGenerator`, an adapter for the domain IdGenerator port.
src/infrastructure/error-handler-middleware.ts: `statusFor(error)` is the only place where domain errors are mapped to HTTP status codes.

parsedVerdict.reasoning:
The src/infrastructure module serves one concern: the adapters and composition root that connect the domain and application layers to concrete technology (Express HTTP, in-memory persistence, UUID generation).

- Both repositories implement their domain ports (OrderRepository, ProductRepository) the same way, with a Map store.
- UuidIdGenerator implements the IdGenerator port.
- Both controllers depend only on application use cases, which are passed in through their constructors.
- app-factory.ts is the single composition root, and server.ts is the single entrypoint.
- The rule mapping domain errors to HTTP status codes lives only in error-handler-middleware.ts (statusFor). The controllers never map errors themselves; they hand errors to next.
- No file goes around the repositories or use cases to reach state directly.

One small inconsistency: order-controller.ts defines a private `wrap` helper that passes async errors to next, while stock-controller.ts writes the same logic inline with `.then(..., next)`. That is two copies of one convention, but they behave the same and the error-status invariant is still in one place. I judged it too minor to count as a fail.
